Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh with a matching frame cap gives smooth, tear-free gameplay at a comfortable medium-low quality level; FSR upscaling from 1024x640 keeps the image reasonably sharp on the Deck screen. Drop Max Background Characters to 10 if frame rate becomes unstable in populated zones.

profiles.Summary: Lost Ark is an online-only action MMO that runs on DirectX 11; the Steam Deck's GPU sits roughly at the game's minimum spec, making 30 fps at low settings achievable in most content but crowded towns and large raid environments will cause noticeable dips. The Playable rating and bronze/trending-gold ProtonDB tier reflect launcher and anti-cheat friction on first setup, but the game is generally functional once running.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs relative to the Deck's GPU class and the bronze/trending-gold ProtonDB tier. On first launch, verify GE-Proton resolves the launcher, then check frame rate in a crowded city hub — if it drops below 25 fps, switch to Max Battery and lower Max Background Characters.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling and a 7 W TDP cap keeps power draw low for longer sessions; a 30 fps cap at 40 Hz reduces tearing and smooths frame pacing. Reducing Max Background Characters further to 5 can help in the busiest city hubs.

KnownIssues: GameGuard anti-cheat and the Smilegate launcher have historically caused launch failures on Proton — GE-Proton is the most commonly recommended workaround.
Crowded areas such as major cities and raid lobbies can cause severe frame drops even at low settings due to high character and particle counts.
The game requires a persistent internet connection and may fail to authenticate or disconnect unexpectedly under some Proton configurations.
Some UI elements and text may be small or poorly scaled for the 1280x800 screen; the game does not have full controller support listed.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 at full TDP can reach 60 fps in open-world and dungeon content, but expect drops to 40-50 fps in crowded cities and large group content; the 60 fps cap prevents the GPU from running unconstrained. Battery life is short at 15 W — best used while plugged in.

Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz delivers noticeably smoother motion than 30 fps and is more sustainable than chasing 60; medium textures improve readability without hitting the GPU hard. Drop to Max Battery settings if frame rate dips persist in raids or crowded hubs.

profiles.Summary: Lost Ark runs on the Steam Deck at its minimum PC spec threshold, making 30 fps achievable at low settings with FSR upscaling, though crowded zones and raid encounters with heavy particle effects can cause noticeable dips. The game is rated Playable (not Verified), requires extra Proton setup steps to get past the launcher and EasyAntiCheat, and controller support is limited enough that Steam Input remapping is strongly recommended.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1050 Ti class GPU, matching the Deck) and general Steam Deck hardware capability. On first run, check frame rate in a major city or raid and switch to the Max Battery profile if it dips below 25 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 significantly reduces GPU load; the 8 W TDP and manual GPU clock keep thermals and battery draw low for extended sessions. Expect occasional dips below 30 fps in heavily populated towns and large raids.

KnownIssues: EasyAntiCheat and the Smilegate launcher can prevent the game from launching under default Proton — GE-Proton is widely recommended to bypass these issues.
Frame rates drop significantly in crowded areas such as major cities, world bosses, and large-scale raids due to heavy particle and character draw calls.
The game is rated Playable, not Verified — controller/gamepad support is incomplete and many menus and ability slots require keyboard/mouse or careful Steam Input remapping.
On-screen UI text and ability icons can be very small at 1280x800; use the in-game Adjustable Text Size accessibility option to compensate.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 with full TDP unlocked squeezes out the best frame rates the Deck can sustain in open-world and dungeon content, but 60 fps is not stable in raids or cities — consider dropping to the 40 fps Optimal profile for those activities. Battery life is short at this power level.
